paper_metadata.title: Portfolio Optimization Based on Quantum HHL Algorithm

summary: The paper applies the HHL quantum linear‑systems algorithm to a toy portfolio optimization problem with 3 assets, reformulated as an 8×8 linear system implemented in a 9‑qubit quantum circuit. The HHL approximate solution (0.1608, 0.2557, 0.5833) closely matches the classical exact solution (0.16216216, 0.25675676, 0.58108108), demonstrating feasibility on a small instance but without runtime comparison or real‑hardware execution.

experiments.description: Portfolio optimization formulated as a quadratic programming problem with equality constraints and solved using the HHL algorithm on IBM's quantum computing platform via Qiskit; the paper reports a 3-asset toy instance and compares the approximate quantum solution to the exact classical solution.

algorithm.variant: HHL for portfolio optimization / quadratic programming with equality constraints

problem_formulation.encoding_details: The linear system derived from the constrained portfolio optimization is embedded into a quantum linear-systems problem A|x⟩=|b⟩; the paper expands the 3-asset instance to an 8-dimensional vector so that 3 qubits can represent |b⟩ and A is expanded to 8×8.
problem_formulation.objective_function: minimize ω^T Σ ω subject to μ^T ω = μ0 and P^T ω = ξ
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Equality constraints are converted to a linear system using Lagrange multipliers; the HHL algorithm is then applied to the resulting linear system.

problem_instance.description: Toy portfolio optimization instance with 3 assets, average returns μ=(0.05, 0.1, 0.2), correlation matrix Σ=[[1,0.5,0],[0.5,1,0.1],[0,0.1,1]], target return μ0=0.15, and total capital ξ=1.

dataset_specification.description: Synthetic 3-asset example; no market dataset or date range reported.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: The 3-asset problem is reformulated into a linear system via the Lagrange method; the input vector b is padded with zeros to 8 dimensions for the quantum circuit.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: The paper compares the normalized approximate solution from HHL with the exact classical solution and reports the ratio of solution components.

implementation_details.classical_solver: Classical exact solution for comparison; no named classical optimization package reported
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Formulation of the portfolio optimization as a constrained quadratic program and conversion to a linear system using Lagrange multipliers; padding to 8 dimensions for qubit encoding.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Measurement of the ancilla qubit; when the ancilla is 1, the amplitudes on the solution register are interpreted as the approximate portfolio weights and normalized.

speedup_claims.conditions: HHL background discussion; not demonstrated on this specific portfolio instance
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper cites the general HHL exponential speedup for linear systems, but does not derive a problem-specific asymptotic speedup for the portfolio instance.

speedup_claims.caveats: The paper does not derive a problem-specific asymptotic speedup for the portfolio example; it only states that HHL provides exponential speedup for linear systems in general.

speedup_claims.caveats: The paper reports a speculative HHL speedup claim in general terms, but does not demonstrate an empirical speedup for the portfolio instance.

speedup_claims.caveats: The paper discusses exponential speedup in the HHL context generally, but does not provide a problem-specific empirical speedup for the portfolio instance.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: Exponential speedup for linear systems is discussed in the HHL background; no problem-specific asymptotic bound is derived for this portfolio instance.

advantage_assessment.crossover_size: not reported; demonstration limited to a 3‑asset toy instance expanded to an 8×8 linear system
advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Practical advantage would require large-scale fault‑tolerant quantum computers capable of implementing HHL with many logical qubits and deep phase‑estimation circuits.
